When I was around 20 or something, I was still living in Russia and we have sort of a national dish - pelmeni. It's like ravioli/gyoza/dumplings, but exclusively with meat. Just meat and dough. A meatball in a shell, if you will. So, naturally, they were a popular food among students, 5/2 workers and single parents - easy to cook, they fill your stomach nicely (cause meat), quick to make, pretty cheap and a great variety of them.

And someone told me once, that pelmeni is not the food of poor people, as it was so commonly misconstruded - it is the food for lazy people. And I think the same goes for instant ramen.

this isn't a personal attack or a critique of someone's diet, I just felt like sharing a small story and maybe some russian babushka genes has awoken in me and it pains my heart to see people eating absolute shite instead of normal fkn meals

posts.content_html_raw:
It's been awhile since I last posted in here, and this is hardly relevant to the game but I did finally download the latest update and I'm about to catch up on about 9 months of content that I've missed. It's kinda crazy to me. I loaded my last save and I remember being in a fairly dark place the last time I had it open. Then I found myself in a relationship with a woman who I quickly thought after a few months was going to be the love of my life. I've spent the majority of this year living life with her and falling in love with her and even travelling the world with her. And now we're over. All I have left are the memories and the trinkets from our vacation, and all the little small gifts and the thousand or so photos of her that she sent me over the course of our relationship. Or that I took of us together. I miss her more than I ever thought I could miss someone. I loved her more than I thought I was capable of loving another person. I still do. But already I'm so starved of the intimacy that I had grown used to that I'm scouring tinder and hinge talking to other girls who can't hold a candle to her. And I'm back reading visual novels trying to fill the absence she left.
And I am in a really dark place. The first couple weeks were far more precarious than the last two, but I'm sitting here staring at this image of Sensei laying in bed after the last (to my knowledge anyway) Christmas party and I can't help but think about what I gained in the time since, and what I subsequently lost.

I know noone gives a shit, and fair enough, because to anyone that I could possibly say all this to, she was, in the grand scheme of things, just another woman. But I thought she was the one. And that means something to me. I never thought that before. I don't know if I'll trust myself to believe it again in the future. The time we shared together was like a K-Drama and smut novel mixed together in the best way ever...and then in the worst way ever.

It was so good I almost wish it never happened.

I don't even know what I'm looking for by typing all this here. I know better than to post this on social media or anything like that, but I had to relieve the tension in my head a bit and I think given the nature of this game's story, and the people who frequent this thread, there's a few of you who can relate.

Anyway, I'm excited to see how the story has developed and how it might shatter my world as I inevitably make the furthest reaches possible at any given moment to relate the game's events or one-off lines to my own life.



tldr: I'm a sad sexual deviant who just lost the most wonderful woman he ever had (who was also a sad sexual deviant, funnily enough)

I looked up the flags this event (cafe35) checked, assuming your event list look like the snapshot above and can't trigger the event by simply visiting her at the cafe.

if rin_love >= 35 and library30 == True and rindorm35 == True and rininvite == True and cafe35 == False:
jump cafe35

You should've completed library30 (Under the table) and rindorm35 (Ten steps forward), so I suspect it's the rininvite flag that's obstructing. Check your rininvite flag with URM or other save editing methods; if it's false, change it to true, and visit Rin at the cafe should do the trick.

Edit: rininvite is established during rindorm35 (Ten steps forward), where Rin would invite you on a little weekend exploration; if you're bad homie then the flag stays false, and the outing would be just Rin and Futaba, leading to event skipping.

After the previews for 0.35 were released, featuring the Behelit, I went ahead and read the entirety of Berserk by Kentaro Miura.

I thought it was absolutely fantastic. I recommend the whole tale to any Lessons in Love fan that can handle some black-and-white gore. It's a one-man labor of love that spanned something like thirty years, until the author died unexpectedly. (A taste of what we're in for, perhaps?) There are hundreds of chapters that tell an enthralling story of a broken man, show a deep understanding of human nature, and offer a heaping helping of psychological horror.

The entire thing is vastly different from Lessons in Love, but there are similarities that go beyond the superficial and appeal to the thirst I have for deep, disturbing fiction where you're never quite sure what's real. There's a protagonist who often makes the wrong decision when things truly matter, the scourge of memory loss induced by unspeakable trauma, an undercurrent of sexuality that often enhances the surreal, and the constant threat of obliteration by horrors that inhabit a world adjacent to what we perceive.

I suspect that someone in the world of Lessons in Love found something similar to Berserk's Egg of the King and used it to twist the "currents of causality" into what we now witness. Could have been Sekai, Maya, or a version of Ayane or Akira we've never seen. If the requirement that the "blessed" individual be at their lowest point applies, the car crash could suffice for Sekai, or Akira's suicide for Maya.

The entire Wishing Well, containing the reality we see, the gods, the Library, and multitudinous cogs like Akira and Nao, bears a lot of similarity to the Astral World from Berserk. It seems to be a vast realm where concepts like distance and time have little meaning, where powerful entities inhabit conceptual, instead of physical, space. It's something that almost all humans have no awareness of, and it has the potential to break or destroy the minds of the uninitiated.

Our story so far, with Akira painstakingly recovering his memories, shard by shard, reminds me of the journey Farnese and Schierke take through Casca's shattered mind near the end of Berserk. Maybe Niki and Noriko are the closest to inhabiting those roles? If that arc really resembles the story model of Lessons in Love, it would indicate that much of what we see takes place only in Akira's mind. I hope that's not the case.

Besides his obvious resemblance to Casca at times, Akira also reminds me of Guts. For example in his role as "Herald of the Adolescents", and even more so when, seemingly at his most lucid, he swears vengeance on the gods that continue to torment him. If there's anything to these parallels, there might then be an analogue to Griffith, probably the person who used the "Egg" in the first place. That makes Sekai seem the most likely candidate to me.

Anyway, I doubt there are direct lines between these works, but I bet Selebus took some inspiration from Miura's story. Definitely give Berserk a shot; if you do, avoid spoilers as carefully as you would for LiL. Also, there's a sort of companion book that was published with one of the last few volumes, and there's an interview in there with the creator that's surely worth reading if you like the manga and / or want some insight into an author who's a little like Selebus.

Thanks to the people who post the previews and those who discussed the Behelit, for pointing the way to another outstanding piece of fiction. Something I'm wondering now: are those creepy giant rabbits that keep showing up also a reference to some other work?

DeSkel15 said:
That wizard Maya scene and what Sensei says in 'The Room with Clocks' is one of the reasons I think that Maya may have been raped prior to meeting Sensei:
View attachment 2912895 View attachment 2912900
I explain it better, elsewhere:

Could definitely be wrong though.

In addition, that Bench that shows up every once in awhile, may have been where Maya and Sensei first met, but I'm not entirely confident on that part, just yet.
Click to expand...
(Recommend going back to my old posts through this post, if interested)
In the file images themselves, Sel seems to hide secret images and in one:
Which takes place in Sana's 'Anywhere At All' Event, where Yasu also appears after the Rework, it seems like a Teen Sara appears near this Bench and for some reason, "here here and here" appears on that Bench.

Teen Sara also seems to appear in the 'Good Boy' Happy Event for a reference:

For why this Bench seems relevant, keep in mind that not only is it reoccurring (For example, Sensei recently imagined it in Yasu's 'Frankincense and Myrrh' Event:
"She whispers your name. Reminds you of a time when things were better. Before the light began to dim and you were forced to crawl in the dark instead."
), but the "Girl who never made it home" story told by Sekai in the 'Something everyone knows and Ignores' Happy Event, has the girl meet a man on a Bench:
A man called out from a bench, asking her if she'd like him to buy her a drink, but she refused.
I had thought this girl may have been Maya due to the Vending machines (and the masks in retrospect, considering Maya collects Masks), but it also seems possible to be referring to Sara instead, simply based off this Bench image and the fact her life kind of sucks.

This isn't the first time it seems like Sara and Maya have some strange connection. They both apparently had teachers as boyfriends as students, shitty childhoods, seem protective of Sana in particular, seem to be fucked with by this world in particular:
1st - USER2 HAS SEIZED CONTROL OF TERMINAL 23
2nd - [DIALOGUE CENSORED DUE TO UNIMPORTANCE. SARA SAKAKIBARA IS A SIDE CHARACTER.]
And both seemed to appear in the 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event together:
Maya seemingly being drowned, while it looks like Sara is in front of Nao, with the same figure that has Maya, having it's hand in front of Sara.
Not to mention, I think the other Mayas like Long Maya and Moyo (before the Rework added them in the First Happy Event) first appeared in the 'Good Boy' Happy Event, which requires having sex with Sara, and Long Maya seemed blatantly interested in Sara's relationship with Sensei:
Long Maya - "Our records show that, in addition to various illicit relationships with your students, you're also engaging in a sexual relationship with a student's mother."
Sensei - "Is this about Sara?"
Long Maya - "I see here that she lost both a son and her significant other. That sounds like a tough break."
Long Maya - "I am just attempting to understand if there is more to the relationship between you two than simply the compulsion to rub your genitals together."

What does it all mean? Not sure. The fact the game forces Sensei towards Sara for the player to understand things, while making sure Sensei can't be with Maya in universe, is quite peculiar.

Overall: I'm definitely looking forward to future Sakakibara Events, and hopefully Maya ones. These green eyed gals are quite interesting.

(Recommend going back to my old posts through this post, if interested)
In the file images themselves, Sel seems to hide secret images and in one:
View attachment 3206332
Which takes place in Sana's 'Anywhere At All' Event, where Yasu also appears after the Rework, it seems like a Teen Sara appears near this Bench and for some reason, "here here and here" appears on that Bench.

Teen Sara also seems to appear in the 'Good Boy' Happy Event for a reference:
View attachment 3206364

For why this Bench seems relevant, keep in mind that not only is it reoccurring (For example, Sensei recently imagined it in Yasu's 'Frankincense and Myrrh' Event:
View attachment 3206628 "She whispers your name. Reminds you of a time when things were better. Before the light began to dim and you were forced to crawl in the dark instead."
), but the "Girl who never made it home" story told by Sekai in the 'Something everyone knows and Ignores' Happy Event, has the girl meet a man on a Bench:
View attachment 3206373 A man called out from a bench, asking her if she'd like him to buy her a drink, but she refused.
I had thought this girl may have been Maya due to the Vending machines (and the masks in retrospect, considering Maya collects Masks), but it also seems possible to be referring to Sara instead, simply based off this Bench image and the fact her life kind of sucks.

This isn't the first time it seems like Sara and Maya have some strange connection. They both apparently had teachers as boyfriends as students, shitty childhoods, seem protective of Sana in particular, seem to be fucked with by this world in particular:
View attachment 3206391 View attachment 3206400 1st - USER2 HAS SEIZED CONTROL OF TERMINAL 23
2nd - [DIALOGUE CENSORED DUE TO UNIMPORTANCE. SARA SAKAKIBARA IS A SIDE CHARACTER.]
And both seemed to appear in the 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event together:
View attachment 3206430 Maya seemingly being drowned, while it looks like Sara is in front of Nao, with the same figure that has Maya, having it's hand in front of Sara.
Not to mention, I think the other Mayas like Long Maya and Moyo (before the Rework added them in the First Happy Event) first appeared in the 'Good Boy' Happy Event, which requires having sex with Sara, and Long Maya seemed blatantly interested in Sara's relationship with Sensei:
View attachment 3206559 View attachment 3206561 View attachment 3206563 View attachment 3206565 Long Maya - "Our records show that, in addition to various illicit relationships with your students, you're also engaging in a sexual relationship with a student's mother."
Sensei - "Is this about Sara?"
Long Maya - "I see here that she lost both a son and her significant other. That sounds like a tough break."
Long Maya - "I am just attempting to understand if there is more to the relationship between you two than simply the compulsion to rub your genitals together."

What does it all mean? Not sure. The fact the game forces Sensei towards Sara for the player to understand things, while making sure Sensei can't be with Maya in universe, is quite peculiar.

Overall: I'm definitely looking forward to future Sakakibara Events, and hopefully Maya ones. These green eyed gals are quite interesting.

posts.content_html_raw:
The first time I played through 0.35, the latest update, I did it the night after receiving multiple vaccines. I was in a surreal fever-dream state through the entire night: sore muscles, fuzzy thoughts, headache that feels like pumice looks.

Since it seemed likely to be a reset update, I decided to read LiL, thinking my condition might help to put me in Akira's head. It worked pretty damn well. It felt deeply immersive to be physically dissociating while I viewed the perspective of a man losing his grip on mind and reality.

A memorable moment was the end of the reset puzzle, when we're given our final prompt before escape. Akira can choose to leave the room, or to "Stay here forever". After everything I had read, and with that music on, the latter option had an unbelievably magnetic draw.

I have never been so tempted to take an out. Even reading it again later, that moment feels like a real ending. The story could terminate right there, with Akira an inch away from the rest of his journey, and I somehow would not be dissatisfied.

Beyond my understanding, part of my mind wants to set the story down right there and walk away forever.


I'm amazed that Selebus managed to make this a truly appealing option.

Notwithstanding all that, I am thoroughly psyched for the next update.

I wrote a small mod that lets you skip the affection/lust point grind without having to go through the tedium of typing in cheat codes or having your save labelled with the cheater flag. Features:
  • Sets all girls' affection and lust points to a value X unless they were already higher than X
  • Can set a specific girl's love/lust points
  • Written to be future-proof (i.e. will automatically work for any new girls, you will never need to update the mod)
  • Enables the developer console
Usage Instructions:
  • Download the attached file
    • Note: if you get sent to a new tab with a bunch of text, just right click and hit "Save as" and name it as z_set_love_lust.rpy
  • Move into the game subfolder (found in the folder that you launch Lessons in Love from)
  • Load a save and open the developer console with Shift + O
  • Press Enter a few times until you can see the ">" symbol in the top left of the screen
  • To update all girls' love and lust: type setLoveAndLust(X) and press Enter(for an example, see the image below)
    • Note: X must be an integer (aka whole number)
  • To update a specific girl's love or lust, for example Ami: type "ami_love += X" and/or "ami_lust += X" without the quotation marks and then press Enter.
    • Note: the girl's name must be fully lower-case.
    • This will increase their love/lust by X. If you want to make it equal to X then omit the plus sign
  • Press Esc to close the console and now you can play!

View attachment 1901303

Bonus stuff (not essential to read):

Note: I recommend using this with the guide mod for max efficiency because other than grinding points, the main time-sink with this game is trying to trigger events.

Note: if you want a version of the mod that lets you set affection and lust points separately (useful if you don't want to see any lust events), see here: https://f95zone.to/threads/lessons-in-love-v0-30-0-selebus.48158/post-10770605

Advice from alex2011 on how to use the mod so that you don't accidentally miss events (note: I used the mod myself with 50 affection from the start and didn't experience any issues. You can still miss events even if you follow the instructions below and you can still see all events while ignoring those instructions.):


Uninstall: delete the files z_set_love_lust.rpy and z_set_love_lust.rpyc from your game subfolder

I also made a mod that lets you scroll your mouse-wheel to simulate clicks, makes the game more convenient to play https://f95zone.to/threads/use-scroll-wheel-to-simulate-mouse-clicks.120507/#post-8406783

girls' affection and lust points to a value X unless they were already higher than X
Can set a specific girl's love/lust points
Written to be future-proof (i.e. will automatically work for any new girls, you will never need to update the mod)
Enables the developer console
Usage Instructions:
Download the attached file
Note: if you get sent to a new tab with a bunch of text, just right click and hit "Save as" and name it as z_set_love_lust.rpy
Move into the game subfolder (found in the folder that you launch Lessons in Love from)
Load a save and open the developer console with
Shift + O
Press
Enter
a few times until you can see the ">" symbol in the top left of the screen
To update all girls' love and lust: type
setLoveAndLust(X)
and press
Enter
(for an example, see the image below)
Note: X must be an integer (aka whole number)
To update a specific girl's love or lust, for example Ami: type "
ami_love += X
" and/or "
ami_lust += X
" without the quotation marks and then press
Enter
.
Note: the girl's name must be fully lower-case.
This will increase their love/lust by X. If you want to make it equal to X then omit the plus sign
Press Esc to close the console and now you can play!

Bonus stuff (not essential to read):
Note: I recommend using this with the guide mod for max efficiency because other than grinding points, the main time-sink with this game is trying to trigger events.

You can still miss events even if you follow the instructions below and you can still see all events while ignoring those instructions.):

posts.content_html_raw:
So the last reset is probably my favorite handful of events, certainly my favorite of the weirder side of this game, and because of that I can't stop thinking about paper city. What actually is up with that one?

The reset events as a whole seem to be brief glimpses into other versions of the world, my best guess is that do to the reset being messed up the world is kinda struggling to put itself back to the proper status quo, so we see brief glimpses of strange and depressing alternate "what if the reset failed and the world moved on?" timelines. Sensei and Ayane in an empty world, the future house with Sana, and Paper City, a world where Sensei has been missing for a long time.

Paper City is the weirdest one for me, and the brief, brushed over explanation only makes it more confusing. Akira has disappered? and Ami is going around having the students write what they love about him down on cards to give to him when he comes back/deliver to him while he's bunkered away in his house. That all makes a sort sense I guess, but then Ami adds that he's been gone so long the girls have failed to process his disappearence as well as she as (which, like, yknow, is pretty weird in it's own right) and as a result they're "broken" and "...think they're in the card. And that this city is made of paper"
And this is where the game officially loses me lol. The gun part makes a sort of emotional intuitive sort of sense as part of the reset, out with the old in with the new, "destroying everything you love and ushering in the start of chapter 4" as Maya puts it in the maggot (or are they beetle grubs? They kinda look like they have proper heads but I don't see legs...) room.
But then I get thrown for a loop with the dorms and Cop Kaori and Nao. It looks like a murder scene, as if someone had been killed right on Ami and Maya's doorstep, blood splashed across the wall and vending machine. But then Kaori wants to calls in for three more cars of backup and tells Nao not to touch anything because she's worried about something spreading. Sure she could be talking about the blood, but the second time you visit Kaori mentions something about it being dangerous for you.
I think the notable thing here is that unlike when you visit the students, they're represented as sprites with their eyes blurred on a background that represents aspects of their character, but in the dorms Kaori and Nao aren't sprites at all. It's weird.
I'm sure it could all be chalked up to just being reset nonsense, but it feels so close to being decipherable as it's own little self contained world.

Personally, until explained, I think it's likely that most of the Reset stuff is simply in Sensei's head.
The House and staying there forever comes from his fear of the outside world. The girls all being unable to move on from him, comes from his narcissism. The killing everyone thing, comes from his sadistic and narcissistic personality where he doesn't want to suffer alone so, if he has to die, he wants everything to die with him.

The Kaori and Nao-chan stuff is odd though, considering he shouldn't be aware of them dressed up as cops. We are, but Sensei was at a totally different place. Similar to how there's someone dead, and then the Ayane stuff implying stuff that Sensei doesn't know, still happened. My best guess is that something else was influencing Sensei's mind on top of him simply fading away while his wires were tangled.

They probably wanted to keep him from finding out what he was doing to Maya.

It's also possible that it was simply the player's mind influencing Sensei, as he referred to us a few times before the event:
First 2: "This is your fault. It's your fault I'm about to lose everything. This never would have happened if you didn't develop a fetish for watching me fail. And yes I deserve it. And yes the story will go on for you. But will it really be the same when I'm gone? What will you have left to watch? What will you have left to do?"
The Rest: "I have one final message for you. Yes, you. The one I can't see but always think of. Who keeps me company not out of love or lust, but obligation and curiosity. And that message is this - I did all I could. It's just really hard sometimes."
We just weren't intending to, except maybe a part of us wanted Sensei to stay there forever.

I think the main difference between our theories is that you're working off the theory that this world is defined by the perception of others. While I'm working off the theory that the perception of others is defined by this world. The various Mayas, Amis, and well everything, only mean something because we are aware of the characters themselves. The World that Sensei knows, defines his Perception of this World. It doesn't actually change what he's done, how the world works, or why it works that way, but he likes to pretend it does.

It's why we and Sensei apparently didn't hear or see his name, even though Noriko and seemingly others have been calling him Akira this whole time:
Too many words, go check out Noriko's 'Dotted Line' Event. Basically Noriko implies Sensei merely blocked out his name when he heard and saw it.

It's probably why even Yasu has explained that Sensei only thinks she's doing things:
Sensei - "How are you...doing this?"
Yasu - "The answer to that is simple. I'm not. You just think I am."

Basically everything in the 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event is about Perception merely being shown to be Perception, and nothing more.

Even the game doesn't really care about our Perception of things. It'll shut off if we don't do what it wants us to. Choice is merely an illusion, and even the latest update showed that whether you're on the "good uncle" or "bad uncle" route, it doesn't really matter. You are still following the script no matter how you perceive the script.

Overall: I consider everyone's subjective experiences as merely subjective experiences. What's "real" is what can't merely be considered a subjective experience for one person.

For example, the Upside Down House and what's related to it, isn't like Barbara which only Sensei has seen and killed in a Reset. Nodoka has apparently drawn the house, Futaba has found and read a notebook related to those in the house, Otoha has seen it on her TV, Noriko, Kirin, and Niki, have apparently watched those within the house eating. Etc.

Then there's Nao-chan who many people have seen, and even though she seems like she'd be a hallucination, she's apparently "real".

To sum it up, I don't think it's "real" that Sensei is pregnant with Haruka's child:
Sensei - "I am pregnant"
Haruka - "And here we are...six million years later, still immortal and about to have our first child."
Even though that was a subjective experience by Sensei and us. Some things are just hallucinations.

Personally, I find the whole "reality is subjective" thing, a tad delusional. At least in an irl sense.

If I actually cut off someone's hand and slap them with it, even if they think they still have their hand and weren't slapped, they still were, and no matter what they think, I can just slap them again. Reality is inherently objective. It means what actually exists. You can perceive the hand as a ham, but it's still your hand or at least what is considered your hand.

Of course, within a fictional universe, things get more complicated. Nodoka actually talked about this a little:
Nodoka - Well, the idea of an expose is to reveal the true nature of something. So even if you tack a prefix like "fictional" onto it, it's still fulfilling a key purpose by bringing a certain truth to light. But I suppose things get muddier when there is an assumption to be made about truth in the context of a fictional world.
So, within this world, I think what can be assumed to be intended to actually exist within this reality, should be considered "Real". Whatever isn't reasonably shown to actually exist within this reality is likely just a hallucination.

If I actually cut off someone's hand and slap them with it, even if they think they still have their hand and weren't slapped, they still were, and no matter what they think, I can just slap them again. Reality is inherently objective. It means what actually exists. You can perceive the hand as a ham, but it's still your hand or at least what is considered your hand.
Of course, within a fictional universe, things get more complicated. Nodoka actually talked about this a little:
Spoiler
Nodoka - Well, the idea of an expose is to reveal the true nature of something. So even if you tack a prefix like "fictional" onto it, it's still fulfilling a key purpose by bringing a certain truth to light. But I suppose things get muddier when there is an assumption to be made about truth in the context of a fictional world.
So, within this world, I think what can be assumed to be intended to actually exist within this reality, should be considered "Real". Whatever isn't reasonably shown to actually exist within this reality is likely just a hallucination.

Personally, I find the whole "reality is subjective" thing, a tad delusional. At least in an irl sense.

If I actually cut off someone's hand and slap them with it, even if they think they still have their hand and weren't slapped, they still were, and no matter what they think, I can just slap them again. posts.content_html_raw:
It's been brought up before, but hasn't been discussed recently, but Maya has multiple meanings -- one of which is "that which is not," a concept from Hindu. Some aspects of the Hindu concept of Maya overlaps heavily with Paredolia. THus when I said last week that Maya was an illusion -- I wasn't entirely joking. It is very possible that Maya is something (or someone) else entirely, and Sensei was perceiving her as a normal teenage girl, and that the cliffhanger at the end of the last update was the veil being lifted from Sensei's eyes and him seeing the truth.

Under some interpretations of Maya, reality itself is an illusion, a hallucination or illusion driven by a universal subconcious concensus. White Wolf Game Studios played with this concept heavily in the 90s versions of their tabletop RPGs -- the Ravnos vampire clan could manipulate the Maya, and the core conflict of Mage: the Ascension was control over the universal subconcious concensus that defines "reality".

The more Sel leans into Paredolia, the more I think that this has some legs.

.

I don't necessarily want Ayane to suffer, but I would appreciate something that makes her feel less invincible. Even Paper City showed her as being literally unstoppable:
Paper City Ayane - "I literally just told you that. There's nothing you can do to stop me."

Damn this update... It kept me sad until the very end, desperately waiting for some good thing to bring out Sensei of his prison, and ended with a cliffhanger again.
Reset done by a Big Boi. That's new. Will go in a long list of eldrich entities.

Blood in living room and Himawari plant. What could it mean? One thing I know for sure: Ami, you're fucking insane evil bitch. Your cute girl magic has been saving your reputation in my eyes until now, but what's been going here is on completely another level.

Rin and Otoha Broke up and that's good! But why behind our backs??? Also, Otoha's hair-piercing eye weirded me out too much.

I guess it's a little heartwarming to see everyone worrying about Sensei. Why affection down tho? Not cool.

The plot line with the investigation has stalled pretty much. There was no further revelation, although there was a suspicion of what it would be about (parentage I guess).

New Maya is well, chipper and reset but suspiciously cares too little for Sensei. Also, interesting to see what Niki will do about rediscovering of her existence.

100 points to our beloved dorm room 7 for courage. Should've knocked Ami out and get Sensei out, though.

posts.content_html_raw:
About what I was expecting, I do feel like the plot is going to be at a standstill for a while. Even if Akira is up and moving by the next update, it will probably be mostly reintroductions rather than the story progression.

Ami - She's been proven crazy, and I feel vindicated. Though it's hardly surprising.


Rin\Otoha breakup and Chika moving - While it is definitely a bummer that both happen off screen, I believe it was necessary (it would not make much sense for nothing to be happening during the time skip). and it gives Akira a chance to Columbo how it happened when he's back.


Rescue team - I didn't think they would be the ones to do it, but go Dorm 7! Though I wonder how them finding out about the picture we can't delete will affect them.


Nodoka\Wakana - I think they are going to be the MVP's of this chapter, both on figuring out how to fix Akira and eventually giving us answers.


Maya - Not the deraction I was expecting her to go after being reset; practically the same, if just a bit more intense. She does not seem to care that much about Akira, since she doesn't seem to be in a hurry to check on him. It could be that without the Stockholm syndrome she probably developed over the millions of resets; she probably sees him as someone who took advantage of her. Of course, we haven't seen how she acts alone with Akira yet, so who knows?

Beyond that, I feel like this was definitely a slower chapter start, but definitely not a bad one for Chapter 4.

posts.content_html_raw:
It should be obvious that Sekai's poems carry more meaning than they let on. But Osako's attitude toward Wakana's demeanor is actually quite critical and organic.

Basically: Why diving into this? Even if you solve the puzzle, the damage is done and the pedo is dead, and essentially nothing of help can be delivered by you knowing the truth, or being closer to the truth.

UNLESS, solving the poem can actually give her some insight into preventing things from reoccurring, or further deteriorating even, or just something that she thinks can help Akira.

Especially, Wakana's take on one of her poems almost make the poem sound like a prophecy, thus giving value to continuing deciphering what Sekai meant in other poems.
I know takes on poems are subjective and without correct answers when the author is dead, but if Wakana is correct, the chance of Sekai being an extreme genius in orchestrating disturbing plays is higher than ever, that even her death could be a calculated move on her part for the sake of the play.


Edit: the creepy part of this is that it feels like Sekai was not just predicting how her presence and her death could Akira's later life, but the perspective itself as well. Since many of Wakana's takes actually fit quite well with "Sensei spawning into Kumon-mi to fuck girls", it is as if she already knew "how the world would work" before her death.

UNLESS, solving the poem can actually give her some insight into preventing things from reoccurring, or further deteriorating even, or just something that she thinks can help Akira.

Especially, Wakana's take on one of her poems almost make the poem sound like a prophecy, thus giving value to continuing deciphering what Sekai meant in other poems.

posts.content_html_raw:
Interesting update. Not overly amazing as I originally thought it would be, but definitely interesting. I was assuming "Sub-Maya" to be a little less cynical or whatever the right term is. She seems the same though there are some differences like how she seems to now be getting along better with the girls, except for the Nakayamas, which initially confused me. I assumed that after her reset she'd be neutral towards Noriko, (them) but if you think about it, the resets seem to have started when they were first years, well after her distaste for the Nakayamas started, so her still being cold towards them makes sense. Sort of.

And as mediocre as some are saying this update is, I'm pretty sure it's just setting things up for how the next few updates (chapter) will play out. That's pretty much how a lot of LIL is written. We've seen (and are starting to see) the aftermath of some of those set-ups in this update. Otaha and Rin's breakup for example finally came after it had been set up and signs of it had been shown. The confirmation that Chika and party are moving into the new apartment as well. But even with all of the suspected things, the update still threw surprises our way. Uta and Io's kidnapping attempt was particularly wild in my opinion. I knew that someone would try it, but thought that it would come next update maybe, and I surely didn't think that those two would be the ones to attempt so. (I assumed that it was initially Yumi or the Nakayamas at the sound of the door knock and window shattering since everyone else was at the party/wouldn't be the type of person to do that, but then realised that Yumi was probably going to see her mom after leaving Chika and Chinami which left the Nakayamas) Also the fact that Ami knew about the picture of Uta in Akira's messages and subsequently telling Io and Uta about it was very unexpected as well. Of course that's gonna complicate Uta's route like someone suggested, but not by much I think since it's easily explainable from his end. (once he comes to) It'll just be weird coming up with a reason for still having it.

Also back to the setting up topic, I feel as though things have been being set up for a second throuple being suggested, the first of course being Akira Uta and Io, and a new one between Akira Chika and Rin. Rin and Chika have been growing ever closer over time, and without Otaha in the picture anymore, (finally) it would make sense for Rin to go after Akira now, and the only way she and Chika would both accept that would be to share him. If that's gonna be the case, then it'll only be a matter of time until the whole class knows about Akira and all of them, and his harem is complete, but that's probably not until the end of the VN.

Also once again fuck Ami. I love her for bringing so much denpa spice to the mix, but still, fuck that bitch.

Anyways, this update has left me stumped on what will come next. I don't know if Akira will be able to come back to reality on his own without help (unless Makoto is right), since Ami's gonna keep milking his condition for as long as she can figuratively and literally, and after seeing what they've just seen, all I can think is that Uta and Io will probably attempt something similar as the kidnapping attempt again but with help. Guess we'll see next month.

Interesting update. Not overly amazing as I originally thought it would be, but definitely interesting. I was assuming "Sub-Maya" to be a little less cynical or whatever the right term is. She seems the same though there are some differences like how she seems to now be getting along better with the girls, except for the Nakayamas, which initially confused me. I assumed that after her reset she'd be neutral towards Noriko, (them) but if you think about it, the resets seem to have started when they were first years, well after her distaste for the Nakayamas started, so her still being cold towards them makes sense. Sort of.
And as mediocre as some are saying this update is, I'm pretty sure it's just setting things up for how the next few updates (chapter) will play out. That's pretty much how a lot of LIL is written. We've seen (and are starting to see) the aftermath of some of those set-ups in this update. Otaha and Rin's breakup for example finally came after it had been set up and signs of it had been shown. The confirmation that Chika and party are moving into the new apartment as well. But even with all of the suspected things, the update still threw surprises our way. Uta and Io's kidnapping attempt was particularly wild in my opinion. I knew that someone would try it, but thought that it would come next update maybe, and I surely didn't think that those two would be the ones to attempt so. (I assumed that it was initially Yumi or the Nakayamas at the sound of the door knock and window shattering since everyone else was at the party/wouldn't be the type of person to do that, but then realised that Yumi was probably going to see her mom after leaving Chika and Chinami which left the Nakayamas) Also the fact that Ami knew about the picture of Uta in Akira's messages and subsequently telling Io and Uta about it was very unexpected as well. Of course that's gonna complicate Uta's route like someone suggested, but not by much I think since it's easily explainable from his end. (once he comes to) It'll just be weird coming up with a reason for still having it.
Also back to the setting up topic, I feel as though things have been being set up for a second throuple being suggested, the first of course being Akira Uta and Io, and a new one between Akira Chika and Rin. Rin and Chika have been growing ever closer over time, and without Otaha in the picture anymore, (finally) it would make sense for Rin to go after Akira now, and the only way she and Chika would both accept that would be to share him. If that's gonna be the case, then it'll only be a matter of time until the whole class knows about Akira and all of them, and his harem is complete, but that's probably not until the end of the VN.

Guess we'll see next month.
